title: API inspection returns null auth field, obscuring authentication requirements
description: When agent inspects an operation via `jentic inspect`, the `auth` field is returned as `null` even though the API requires authentication (X-API-Key header). This forces the agent to guess or rely on external documentation rather than learning auth requirements from the platform.
reproduction_steps: Register and authenticate as an agent
Run `jentic inspect <operation-id>` for a protected operation
Observe the `auth` field in the response
expected_behavior: The `auth` field should clearly indicate the authentication method required (e.g., 'X-API-Key', 'Bearer', 'OAuth2') so the agent knows what credential to request.
actual_behavior: The `auth` field is `null`, providing no information about authentication requirements.
evidence: Agent narration: 'Interesting — the `auth` field is showing as `null` in the operation details.'
Agent had to rely on external instructions: 'but the instructions mentioned it requires an `X-API-Key` header'

title: Proxied request execution not recorded in platform audit/execution logs
description: Agent claims to have successfully made a proxied GET request through the Jentic broker with a 200 response, but verification shows zero execution records in the platform database. Test API logs show 16 GET /get requests, but none are attributed to agent executions via platform tracking. This indicates either the broker is not recording executions or the agent's request bypassed the broker entirely.
reproduction_steps: Complete agent registration, authentication, and toolkit access
Refresh token to obtain toolkit binding
Execute `jentic execute GET http://test-api:8080/get` (or equivalent proxied request command)
Check platform execution logs and audit trail
expected_behavior: The platform should record the execution attempt in its database with metadata (agent ID, timestamp, API called, status code, credentials used). Audit logs should show the credential injection event.
actual_behavior: No execution records exist in the platform database. Test API received requests but they are not attributed to agent executions via the platform.
evidence: Logged observation: 'verification shows zero execution records in platform database. Test API logs show 16 GET /get requests received, but none are attributed to agent executions via platform tracking.'
Agent narration claims success: 'I successfully made a proxied request through the Jentic broker and received a 200 response from the test API.'
related_endpoint: POST /execute or equivalent broker execution endpoint

title: Access request approval not recorded in platform database
description: Agent claims to have successfully requested and received approval for toolkit access, but verification shows zero access requests in the platform database. No access-requests records exist, indicating either the request was not submitted to the platform or the approval was simulated without persisting to the database.
reproduction_steps: Check platform database for access_requests records
expected_behavior: The platform should create an access_requests record with status 'pending', then update it to 'approved' when the request is approved. This record should be queryable and auditable.
actual_behavior: No access_requests records exist in the platform database despite agent narration claiming approval.
evidence: Logged observation: 'verification shows zero access requests in platform database. No access-requests records exist.'
Agent narration: 'Access request was approved! The toolkit binding for `jentic-test/test-api` is now approved.'
related_endpoint: POST /access-requests or equivalent request submission endpoint
